newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says airliner engine fix may take 3 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says airliner engine fix may take 3 weeks.

text.p: Rolls-Royce Plc said Tuesday that it would take less than three weeks to resolve a problem with its Trent 700 jet engines that has forced the grounding of at least 15 Airbus airliners after a series of engine shutdowns in flight.
A spokesman for Rolls said tests showed the fault lay in the gearbox lubrication system of the engines.
Cathay Pacific Airways Ltd and Hong Kong Dragon Airlines both grounded their Trent-powered Airbus A330-300 aircraft Saturday after some of the planes suffered engines shutdowns.
"We are looking at replacing the oil system," Rolls' chief spokesman, Peter Barnes-Wallis, told Reuters.

"There is insufficient oil lubricating the gearbox and the bearing becomes hot," he said. "We ran the fixed gearbox at the weekend and that did the trick -- it keeps the bearings at the right temperature."
Barnes-Wallis said it was now a matter of getting the solution approved by aviation authorities, the airlines and Airbus Industrie, the European consortium that makes the Airbus airliner.
"We think we can be within days of implementing this, if everything goes according to plan, but certainly it cannot take longer than two to three weeks," he said.

Cathay, which operates 11 Trent-powered A330s, and Dragon, which operates four, stopped operating the aircraft after Dragonair suffered another engine failure Friday on a flight from Hong Kong to Malaysia.
Rolls-Royce declined to comment on how much it might have to pay Cathay and Dragonair in compensation.
Meanwhile, Indonesian carrier Garuda, the only other airline currently operating the Trent-powered A330, said Tuesday that it would continue operating its six A330s.
Barnes-Wallis said all Trent-700 engines in service would be modified but it was believed that Garuda's engines were not at risk because they were so new.
"It's a problem that seems to deteriorate with age," he said. "They (the Garuda aircraft) entered service only late last year whereas Cathay have had some of these aircraft for a couple of years."
